title: Meta staff were ranked by AI use. They gamed it.
subtitle: Big tech companies started ranking staff by how much AI they used, and staff set AI to work on nothing to climb the charts. Why counting AI use backfires, and what to count instead.
youtube_title: Meta staff were ranked by AI use. They gamed it.
youtube_description:
In 1902, Hanoi paid people for every rat tail they handed in. So people snipped the tails off live rats, let them go, and some even farmed rats. The city got tails, and more rats.

In 2026, Meta and Amazon ran leaderboards that ranked staff by how much AI they used. Staff set AI agents running on pointless tasks to climb them, and both boards came down. And when one company halved its AI target, most of the junk vanished and its sales staff sold 7% more.

Whatever you count, people learn to produce. If you're counting how much AI your people use, you're counting rat tails.

The full deep dive is at makeyourmindup.ai
